videos.title: My product design process – a walkthrough of the Double Diamond UX Design Process
videos.why: A working product designer walks through both diamonds and the methods she reaches for in each phase; notice how much happens before a single screen is drawn.

videos.title: When is High-fidelity Worth It?
videos.why: Four questions for deciding how polished a piece of process work should be; useful when an AI tool can hand you a finished-looking screen in seconds and tempt you to skip the rough stage.

podcasts.episode: Jake Knapp: Lessons from running 150+ design sprints at Google Ventures
podcasts.why: The creator of the design sprint on squeezing the whole process into one week; listen for how the sprint still starts with understanding the problem and ends with real people trying a prototype.
Two working interface designers try to define a wireframe and argue about when one is worth making; good context for deciding where low fidelity fits in your own process.

reads.title: The Double Diamond
reads.why: The source page from the UK body that created the model, with a short paragraph on each of the four phases; note its point that testing early ideas can send you back to the start, which is normal.

reads.title: UX Prototypes: Low Fidelity vs. High Fidelity
reads.why: Breaks fidelity into visuals, content and interactivity, and says what each level is good for testing; it maps directly onto the fidelity figure.

reads.title: How the discovery phase works
reads.why: How UK government teams run the first diamond in practice, including what they need to learn before building anything; a plain, real-world example of process.
